## Simple explanation

Robotics combines machines, sensors, software, and control so a system can
perceive its surroundings and act on them. AI can help robots recognize
objects, plan routes, or adapt actions.

## Technical explanation

A robotic system integrates sensing, state estimation, planning, control,
and actuation. It may operate under uncertainty and real-time constraints,
with physical dynamics and safety limits. Learning-based components often
work alongside classical estimation and control methods.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Robots connect AI decisions to physical consequences. Engineers must
consider hardware variation, sensor noise, latency, safety, and the gap
between simulation and real-world operation.

## How it works

Sensors provide observations, algorithms estimate state, planners choose
goals or trajectories, and controllers send commands to actuators. Feedback
from new sensor readings closes the loop and allows actions to adapt as the
environment changes.

## Practical example

A warehouse robot can use cameras and range sensors to estimate position,
plan a collision-free route, and adjust wheel speeds as people or obstacles
move into its path.

## Common misconceptions

- Robotics is not only mechanical engineering or only AI; it depends on
  integration across hardware and software.
- A policy that succeeds in simulation may fail on real hardware because
  sensors, dynamics, and environments differ.
